title: delurio UI graph (ui.yaml)
description: What each state of a flow shows, in delurio-graph/0 (SPEC.md §4): the nodes of the screen, their WAI-ARIA roles, accessible names, visible texts and the events they send. Every word a user sees comes from the catalog, by key.

kind.description: The kind of graph file. A ui.yaml is `ui`.

id.description: The UI graph's id; its flow names it with `ui:`.

flow.description: The id of the flow whose states the nodes are shown in.

title.description: The UI graph in plain words, for people.

summary.description: What the screens are, in a few plain sentences.

catalog.description: The catalog the page uses, relative to this file: `catalog/<locale>.json`, a locale being a BCP 47 tag.

locales.description: The locales the UI is written in, as BCP 47 tags; each has a catalog beside `catalog`, named `<locale>.json`.

kit.description: The kit the screens are drawn with (SPEC.md §8), relative to the graph; `--kit` wins.

samples.description: Values for catalog parameters, on the page and in videos: `{client}` in a message is filled with `samples.client`.

task.description: The flow's name as its users know it, in their own words and language, such as "Invite a member": what Rehber names the task by, and what a list of tasks or a video shows. The graph's `title` is in the graph's language, for the people who write it; this is in every locale.

key.description: The catalog key of the name; every locale's catalog must have it.

changes.$comment: exactly one of key or missing
changes.description: What the flow changes and what follows, in its users' own words: what is created, sent, charged or removed, who sees it, and whether it can be undone. Required under --strict when the flow's steps invoke a writing action of its domain: `{ key }`, or `{ missing: <why> }` where the app has no such message yet, a gap that fails nothing (SPEC.md §4).

key.description: The catalog key of the note; every locale's catalog must have it.

missing.description: Why the flow has no changes note yet, such as an app that has no message saying what the flow changes. Rehber does not guide the flow's writing steps, and check gives the gap as a note (changes-note-gap).
examples: the app does not say what an import changes yet

nodes.description: The nodes of the screens, by id. A node is shown in a state when the state is in `in`, not in `unless`, and `when` holds.

propertyNames.description: A node's id: camelCase, and not opener, which a returnsFocus says for the node that opened its dialog (SPEC.md §4).

focus.description: The node that has focus when the flow enters a state from another state, after someone acts or a step ends, by state. A page that opens gives the focus to its `initialFocus` instead, and a dialog that closes to its `returnsFocus` node. The node is shown in that state.

additionalProperties.description: The node that has focus in that state.

edges.description: Relations the page and the checks use: a node labelled by another, an action that leads to a state, the node a dialog gives the focus back to.

rules.description: Rules the screens must keep, in words. Written but no tool reads them yet (#3).

formatVersion.description: The format and its version. Every graph file starts with it.

status.description: `proposed`: written before or apart from the code, nobody has approved it. `captured`: read from existing code (capture mode, every element carries `source`). `approved`: the owner reviewed and accepted it.

identifier.description: An identifier of the graph: English camelCase (SPEC.md §1, Text).

stateRef.description: The id of a state of the flow.

nodeRef.description: The id of a node of this UI graph.

states.description: States of the flow, by id.

expression.description: An expression of delurio's own language (SPEC.md §3) over the flow's context: or, and, not, ==, !=, in, not in, ( ), [lists], 'strings', numbers, true, false, null, and names (a context variable, a named guard of the flow, or `state`).

sourceAnchor.description: A source anchor (SPEC.md §9): `<repo-relative path>:<line>`, or a bare `<path>` for a whole file, naming the code that draws the element.

label.$comment: exactly one of key, labelledBy, literal or oneOf
label.description: Words of a node, in one of these forms: `{ key, params }` from the catalog, `{ labelledBy: <node> }`, `{ literal }`, or `{ oneOf: [keys] }`.

key.description: The catalog key of the message.

params.description: The data each `{param}` of the message stands for (e.g. `client: client.name`); the page fills it from `samples`.

additionalProperties.description: The data the parameter stands for.

labelledBy.description: The node whose text gives these words.

literal.description: Words that are not translated (a product name, a code).

oneOf.description: Catalog keys of which one is shown, depending on the data.

allOf.$comment: params go with key or oneOf

value.$comment: exactly one of key, literal or oneOf
value.description: What a field holds when it is shown, until someone types in it, in one of these forms: `{ key, params }` from the catalog, `{ literal }` (`{ literal: "" }` for an empty field), or `{ oneOf: [keys] }`.

key.description: The catalog key of the message the field holds.

params.description: The data each `{param}` of the message stands for (e.g. `title: note.title`); the page fills it from `samples`.

additionalProperties.description: The data the parameter stands for.

literal.description: What the field holds, as it is; an empty string for an empty field.

oneOf.description: Catalog keys of which one is held, depending on the data.

allOf.$comment: params go with key or oneOf

component.description: A kit-neutral component; a kit maps it to the product's own (SPEC.md §8). A `TextField`'s, a `Checkbox`'s, a `Radio`'s and a `Select`'s `text` is its label, and the control is named by it. A `Checkbox` (role checkbox or switch) and a `Radio` (role radio) say with `checked` whether they are checked; a `Select` (role combobox) is a choice of one option, and its `value` is the option it shows chosen.

role.description: The WAI-ARIA 1.2 role the node exposes; `kit check` reads it from the browser's accessibility tree.

native.description: The HTML control the node is, when WAI-ARIA gives that control no role (HTML-AAM: no corresponding role): an <input> of type date, time, datetime-local, month, week, file or color, or a <summary>. A node that says it gives no `role`, and `role-missing` does not apply to it; a replay and `kit check` find it by its name among controls of that kind (SPEC.md §4).

name.description: The accessible name (Accessible Name and Description Computation 1.2), kept apart from `text` so that "the visible text is in the name" (WCAG 2.5.3) is checkable.

in.description: The flow states the node is shown in.

unless.description: The flow states the node is not shown in.

when.description: A guard or context flag of the flow that must hold for the node to show.

disabledIn.description: The states where the node is shown but disabled.

disabledWhen.description: An expression over the flow's context (SPEC.md §3): where it holds, the node is shown but disabled, in any state that shows it, such as a button that waits until a VAT number is typed or a box is ticked. Beside disabledIn, the node is disabled where either says so. A replay compares it in each situation it stops in.

emits.description: The event the node sends when pressed: an event of the flow, UPPER_SNAKE.

initialFocus.description: On a page: the node that has focus when it opens, at the flow's start or when a transition shows it.

repeat.description: The node is drawn once per item of this data.

frame.description: For a page: whether it may be framed; `never` (served with CSP frame-ancestors 'none').

value.description: On a field: what it holds when it is shown, until someone types in it. A replay reads the field's value and compares it.

holds.description: The field of the flow's domain whose value the node shows, or the control takes: <Entity>.<field>. A node that holds a field whose sensitivity is credential is masked wherever the flow's screens are recorded (SPEC.md §4, §7).

checked.description: On a checkbox, menuitemcheckbox, menuitemradio, option, radio or switch: whether it is checked (or selected) when it is shown, as an expression over the flow's context (SPEC.md §3), or true or false. A replay reads its checked state and compares it.

script.description: On a page: how much of it works without JavaScript. `optional`: the page and its actions (plain forms and links). `actions`: the page is drawn and read without it (rendered on the server), and only its actions need it. Without it, the page needs JavaScript. A replay's second walk with JavaScript off checks an `optional` page and takes its actions, and checks an `actions` page but its actions, and ends there.

allOf.$comment: initialFocus, frame and script are only on a page
value is only on a field: what the field holds
checked is only on a node whose role is checkbox, menuitemcheckbox, menuitemradio, option, radio or switch
native is only on a field or an action
a node that names its native control gives no role: WAI-ARIA gives that control none

edge.description: A relation between nodes: `{ labelledBy: [node, labelNode] }`, `{ triggers: [node, state] }` or `{ returnsFocus: [dialog, node | [node, ..] | opener] }`.

labelledBy.description: A node and the node that labels it.

triggers.description: An action and the state it leads to.

returnsFocus.description: A dialog (a page node whose role is dialog or alertdialog) and the node that has focus when it closes, usually the one that opened it. Where several nodes open the dialog, the list of them, or opener: the focus goes back to the one pressed to open it. It wins over `focus` for the state the dialog closes into, when that state shows the node.

anyOf.description: The node, or opener: the node pressed to open the dialog.
The nodes that open the dialog: the one pressed to open it has the focus.
